Team —

I'm kicking off the "Armada" sizing thread to get a final recommendation for Acme's private GPU pool. Goals: produce a concise matrix we can hand to Acme's infra team that spells out sustained throughput targets, burst headroom, network egress cordon thresholds, and an autoscale policy suitable for their VPC/on‑prem deployment. Acme's specific asks from the scoping call:

- Support 3 customer classes (Pilot / Business / Enterprise) with clear per‑class QPS and p95 latency targets.
- Define sustained vs burst capacity (what we guarantee vs what can be absorbed).
- Network egress cordon: per‑pool egress thresholds that trigger rate‑limiting or canary failover to lower‑egress model variants.
- Warm pool & KV cache guidance so cold starts don’t blow latency targets.

I've attached an initial workload matrix (armada_sizing_model_v1.xlsx) and a simple diagram for the egress cordon. Please review and populate the sheet with: GPU counts, expected tokens/sec, expected p95, egress Mbps per GPU, and recommended warm pool sizes.

Target timeline: we want a one‑pager and the filled spreadsheet by EOD Tue (20 Jan) to include in the customer commitment email.

Primary questions for the sizing pass:
1) For Acme's Business tier (target sustained: 120 qps, p95 250ms at 512 tokens avg) — how many A100-equivalent GPUs, and what's the recommended warm pool?
2) Where should we set the egress cordon threshold per GPU (Mbps) to avoid noisy‑neighbor network saturation while allowing short bursts?
3) What's your suggested autoscale window and buffer (e.g., add 2 GPUs when 85% sustained utilization for 90s)?

Notes: Acme will accept soft SLAs for burst absorption but needs firm sustained commitments.

Thanks —
Laura

Thanks Laura — I populated the sheet and ran a quick sim. Summary below (full numbers in the spreadsheet).

Executive baseline (A100-equivalent perf assumed):
- Pilot: target sustained 20 qps; sizing: 1 GPU; warm pool: 0 (on‑demand); expected p95 ~320ms at 512 tokens
- Business: target sustained 120 qps; sizing: 3 GPUs; warm pool: 1 GPU reserved (to absorb short spikes); expected p95 ~240ms with warm pool
- Enterprise: target sustained 480 qps; sizing: 12 GPUs in 3-node racks; warm pool: 2 GPUs; expected p95 ~180–210ms

Network egress guidance (per GPU):
- Average egress (in our sim) ~ 40–55 Mbps per GPU for 512-token completions at Business throughput.
- Cordon threshold recommendation: 85 Mbps/GPU (soft), 110 Mbps/GPU (hard). When soft is hit, trigger queueing/traffic shaping; when hard is hit, fallback to lower‑egress quantized model variant and throttle new sessions.

Autoscale policy (proposal):
- Metric: token-generation utilization per GPU (proxy via kernels/sec + queue depth).
- Scale up: add a 1‑GPU unit when sustained utilization > 82% for 60s.
- Scale down: remove 1‑GPU unit when utilization < 45% for 180s and queue depth = 0.
- Warm pool: keep 1 reserved GPU per pool for Business tier; Enterprise keep 2. Warm pool spins up to serving state in ~90–120s (network/kernels warm).

Failure modes called out: KV cache cold miss storms on scale‑out -> suggest pre‑warmed cache snapshotting for warm pool. Also, if egress cordon is hit and fallback model is used, latency will change — include transparent header to signal variant.

I've attached sim logs (sim-run-jan15.log) and the updated spreadsheet. I'll add a small section in the spreadsheet with operator runbook steps (cordon detection -> notify -> throttle -> fallback model -> scale decision).

Laura / Jonas — quick follow up after reviewing the sheet. Two operational points to add before we hand to the customer: 

1) KV cache warmup: recommend a two‑tier warmup for the warm pool — SSH kick off a background prefix cache seeding job that replays a small set of representative prompts (we included a seed list in the sheet). That gets effective KV hit rates above 90% within the warm window.
2) Canary & rollback flow: for the egress cordon fallback, include a canary fraction (5%) that is first shifted to low‑egress variant when soft threshold is hit. If canary error rate + hallucination metrics increase beyond threshold for 3 consecutive minutes, rollback to original routing and signal SRE.

Also, one more ask from Acme: they want to see the last‑mile egress plan (what happens on their edge router when we open multiple TCP sessions). I've added a diagram (network-egress-cordon-diagram.png) and short notes in the Drive link.

If everyone signs off, I'll assemble the one‑pager and a short runbook so Ben can send to Acme next week.

Team — solid work, thanks. Executive summary I plan to share with Acme (short version they can publish to procurement):

- Sustained commitments (Business tier): 120 qps sustained at p95 <= 250ms (512 tokens avg) backed by a 3 GPU pool with 1 GPU warm reserve.
- Burst absorption: short bursts up to ~2x sustained handled via warm pool + autoscale; best‑effort beyond that with transparent fallback to quantized low‑egress model variant.
- Network cordon: soft cordon at 85 Mbps/GPU (queue & canary diversion), hard cordon 110 Mbps/GPU (fallback & alert).
- Autoscale: +1 GPU at 82% sustained for 60s; scale down after 180s below 45% with zero queue.
